hero.headline: Commercial Roofs Built To Take A NEPA Winter
hero.subheadline: Flat and low-slope membrane, architectural metal, sheet metal and emergency leak service for buildings across Luzerne, Lackawanna and Monroe counties. Established 1993 — and an Excalibur Award winner every year since 1994.

promise_band.eyebrow: When The Roof Is Already Leaking
promise_band.headline: Two Locations, On-Call Technicians
promise_band.body: When water is coming into occupied space, the cost is the disruption, not the patch. That is why we keep on-call service technicians at both the Nanticoke and Dickson City locations. We get on-site quickly, find where the water is actually entering rather than where it is landing, and stop it. Then you get a straight answer about whether that was a repair or the first sign of something bigger.

signature_system.headline: The Pinnacle Standard
signature_system.intro: Every Pinnacle job runs the same way, whether it is a 200,000 square foot re-roof on a hospital or a single leak at a parapet. The spec is written to the building, the crew is ours, and the warranty is one you can actually call in.

blocks.title: A warranty that is still worth something in year fifteen
blocks.body: Most commercial roof disputes are warranty disputes. Owners find out after a leak that the twenty-year warranty covered the material and not the installation, and that the installer is gone. We are an authorized contractor with manufacturer warranties on every system we install, and we have been in the same market since 1993 to answer the call.

blocks.title: Specified to the building, not to the catalogue
blocks.body: Membrane choice, insulation R-value, fastening pattern and drainage all change with the deck, the occupancy and the exposure. We spec the system to the building in front of us. That is also why we install all types of single-ply rather than selling one product to everybody.

blocks.title: Sheet metal is half the job
blocks.body: Flat roofs almost never fail in the middle of the field. They fail at the parapet, the curb, the scupper and the termination. Sheet metal is in our name because we fabricate and install those details ourselves instead of subbing them out.

about_block.headline: Thirty-Three Years On NEPA Roofs
about_block.body: Paul Eyerman started Pinnacle in 1993. Three decades later the company runs out of two locations — Nanticoke and Dickson City — and the leadership has 100 years of roofing between them. In that time Pinnacle has roofed Geisinger hospitals in Danville, Scranton and Wilkes-Barre, Sanofi Pasteur in Swiftwater, the Tobyhanna Army Depot, Kalahari Resort in the Poconos, Wilkes University, Luzerne County Community College and the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport, among many others.

seo_body.eyebrow: Why NEPA Building Owners Call Us
seo_body.headline: Commercial Roofing In Wilkes-Barre & Scranton
paragraphs: Northeastern Pennsylvania is hard on low-slope roofs. Snow sits on them for weeks, freeze-thaw cycles work at every seam and termination all winter, and ice damming backs water up under flashings that were never detailed for it. Membranes rarely fail in the middle of the field here — they fail at the parapet, the curb and the scupper, which is exactly the work most shingle contractors are not set up to do.

We install all types of single-ply membrane, architectural metal and composite aluminum panel systems, and we fabricate the sheet metal that ties them together. Every system carries a manufacturer warranty, and we register it in your name. For owners chasing operating cost, we are part of the Energy Star Savings Program and install reflective white systems with the insulation specified to the building.

Since 1993 we have worked on hospitals, universities, army depots, banks, schools, resorts, supermarkets, manufacturing plants and municipal buildings across Luzerne, Lackawanna and Monroe counties. If you manage a building in Wilkes-Barre, Scranton, Hazleton or the Poconos, there is a good chance you already know a roof we put on.

faqs.a: No. Pinnacle is a commercial roofing contractor. We work on institutional, industrial, retail, municipal and multi-family buildings — hospitals, schools, churches, plants, banks, shopping centres and industrial parks. If you need a shingle roof on a single-family home, we are not the right call.

faqs.q: What does the warranty actually cover?
faqs.a: Every system we install carries a manufacturer warranty, and we register it in your name rather than leaving it in a folder here. We will tell you in writing, before you sign anything, what term you are getting and what it does and does not cover — including where the material warranty ends and workmanship begins. That is the single most common thing owners find out too late.

faqs.q: My roof is leaking right now. How fast can you get here?
faqs.a: Call the closest location — (570) 735-7751 in Nanticoke or (570) 343-7153 in Dickson City. We keep on-call service technicians at both, and emergency service is something we actively offer rather than fit in around new work. Tell us where the water is showing up inside and what is under it.

faqs.q: Do I need a full replacement or can this be repaired?
faqs.a: Often it can be repaired, and we will tell you when that is the honest answer. What decides it is the condition of the insulation and deck underneath, not the look of the membrane on top. We evaluate the roof, tell you what we found, and quote the repair and the replacement so the decision is yours with the numbers in front of you.

faqs.q: Can a new roof reduce our energy costs?
faqs.a: On a building with a large roof area, yes — often meaningfully. We are part of the Energy Star Savings Program and install reflective white membrane systems with the insulation specified for the building. On a re-roof it is usually the cheapest efficiency upgrade available, because the roof is already open.
